current_row.boundary_rationale: The address turns to a direct vocative at 25:34 -- “Wail, you shepherds, and cry” (web:Jer.25.34), spliced הֵילִ֨ילוּ הָרֹעִ֜ים וְזַעֲק֗וּ (oshb:Jer.25.34, byte tier) -- summoning the shepherds and the leaders of the flock by name, a shift from the third-person judgment scene just closed. The row runs to the close of the chapter: “He has left his covert, as the lion” (web:Jer.25.38), rendering עָזַ֥ב כַּכְּפִ֖יר סֻכּ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.25.38, byte tier). That closing lion image echoes 25:30's own opening, where Yahweh roars “against his fold” (web:Jer.25.30), a repetition that argues for reading 25:30-38 as one sustained piece even though this tiling opens a new row at the shepherds' vocative; the row is held at reduced confidence on that account.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 25:30-38 as one row was considered on the strength of the lion image bracketing both ends of the poem, from the roar against the fold to the lion leaving its den. This tiling discloses that echo without letting it override the vocative shift at 25:34.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A reign-dated bereshit-mamlekhet header opens the row: “In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from Yahweh” (web:Jer.26.1), spliced בְּרֵאשִׁ֗ית מַמְלְכ֛וּת יְהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הָיָה֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.1, byte tier) -- distinct in shape from the cup oracle's own date-and-word-event opening just closed. Yahweh's private instruction to Jeremiah follows: “Stand in the court of Yahweh’s house” (web:Jer.26.2), rendering עֲמֹד֮ בַּחֲצַ֣ר בֵּית יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier), commanding him to speak the full warning without omission, closing on the Shiloh threat, “I will make this house like Shiloh” (web:Jer.26.6), spliced וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier; the verse also carries a ketiv/qere note further on, on the demonstrative for the threatened city, consulted but not spliced here). The command and the content it dictates stay one unit because no scene change separates the header from the instruction it introduces. The row closes at 26:6 because 26:7 turns on a participant and scene change -- the priests, the prophets, and all the people, external and crowd-facing rather than Yahweh's private instruction -- spliced וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֛וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים וְהַנְּבִאִ֖ים וְכָל הָעָ֑ם אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.26.7, byte tier), the ruled seam class that stops this unit here.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 26:1 as a bare header, separate from the instruction that follows, was considered and set aside: the command in 26:2-6 carries the row's substance, delivered in the same private scene the header opens.

current_row.device_notes: Two devices reach across the closing seam without overturning it: the threat closing this row, וְנָתַתִּ֛י אֶת הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה כְּשִׁלֹ֑ה (oshb:Jer.26.6, byte tier; the verse's own ketiv/qere note stands on the demonstrative further on, already disclosed at this row's own close and not repeated here; sweep: 1 verse at skeleton tier for this spelling), is quoted back at כְּשִׁלוֹ֙ (oshb:Jer.26.9, byte tier; sweep: 9 verses at skeleton tier for that spelling, a substring count rather than an exclusive Shiloh tally), inside the house phrase (sweep: 6 verses at skeleton tier, half of them in this chapter); and the charge אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.26.2, byte tier) is reported carried out at אֵ֣ת כָּל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.8, byte tier). Both stand as continuity across the seam rather than evidence against the participant-and-scene-change close. Jer.25.38, just before this row, carries a petuchah, and Jer.26.6, this row's own close, carries a setumah (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets).
